entries.title: Bears-Buccaneers inactives: Bears RB Kyle Monangai remains out with toe injury
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> should get No. 2 running back Kyle Monangai back from a toe injury after the bye week for their Nov. 22 game against the Saints, but he missed his fifth consecutive game Sunday against the Buccaneers.</p><p>The team had listed Monangai as questionable despite being limited in practice Friday, which was his first time on the field since suffering the injury in Week 4 against the Jets, but he was inactive for the Bucs game.</p><p>Monangai was 24th in the NFL in rushing last season with 724 yards and had five touchdowns. He was off to a great start this season with 324 yards and three touchdowns in the first four games.</p><p>At cornerback, Tyrique Stevenson will play through a thumb injury, and Malik Muhammad is out with a toe injury.</p><p>The Bucs made starting outside linebacker Yaya Diaby inactive with a knee injury.</p><p>Here are the Bears' inactives:</p><p>RB Kyle Monangai (toe)<br>QB <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/28/bears-inactives-vs-eagles-k-cairo-santos-cb-tyrique-stevenson-good-to-go" >Case Keenum</a> (listed as emergency third QB)</p><p>DL Jayden Loving<br>LB Keyshaun Elliott<br>CB Malik Muhammad (toe)</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Bears-Bucs notes: Mike Tirico sits out with health issue
entries.summary: <p>NBC play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico, who was slated to call his 300th NFL game Sunday night, was replaced by Noah Eagle. Tirico said in a statement released around noon Sunday that a health issue would prevent him from calling the Buccaneers-Bears game at Soldier Field.</p><p>He said he’d return next week.</p><p>Eagle called the Notre Dame game Saturday night in South Bend, Ind.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="zxx" dir="ltr"><a href="https://t.co/eKyVRb8ZOn">pic.twitter.com/eKyVRb8ZOn</a></p>— NBC Sports PR (@NBCSportsPR) <a href="https://x.com/NBCSportsPR/status/2119495623896400051?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 8, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3>Deadline pressure?</h3><p>The Bears made their biggest splash of their trade season — and maybe the biggest splash in the NFL — when they traded for Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons late last month. They have another day-and-a-half to add to it — the NFL’s trade deadline is at 3 p.m. Tuesday.</p><p>The Bears could use depth at cornerback and defensive end. Cornerbacks Nahshon Wright (Jets) and Riq Woolen (Eagles) have been linked to the Bears, as has edge rusher Khalil Mack. The winless Chargers haven’t indicated they plan to move Mack, who played for the Bears from 2018-21.</p><p></p><h3>Notes</h3><p>• When receiver Rome Odunze caught a touchdown in the first quarter, he paid tribute to injured teammate Cole Kmet by doing his baseball swing celebration. Kmet, who is out for the season with a knee injury, played baseball at Notre Dame.</p><p>• The Bears fans who wanted to support Simmons by wearing orange — to match his sleeves — made a statement. An unscientific glance at the Soldier Field crowd showed more orange than usual.</p><p>• Quarterback Caleb Williams wore bright orange Caddix cleats. Like he did Monday, Williams wore a version with no discernable logo to avoid fines by the NFL.</p><p>• Former all-world returner Devin Hester hyped up the crowd on the field before kickoff.</p><p>• During warmups, the Bears set the play clock to 89 seconds in honor of the late Mike Ditka.</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Blackhawks' first change is at backup goalie: Drew Commesso replaces Arvid Soderblom
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>' first change of hopefully several this week came Sunday as Drew Commesso replaced Arvid Soderblom as the team's backup goalie.</p><p>The move ends Soderblom's run of more than three seasons as the Hawks' backup. The 27-year-old Swede, who is on the second year of a two-year contract and will be an unrestricted free agent next summer, was placed on waivers.</p><p>Commesso, who has been patiently waiting his turn in Rockford for more than three years, now gets a full-time NHL opportunity at last.</p><p>The 24-year-old has struggled early this season in the AHL, going 2-4-1 with an .890 save percentage. But he proved himself a solid AHL goalie each of the past three seasons. </p><p>He impressed in three Hawks starts last season, too, going 2-1-0 with a .918 save percentage — including a heroic shutout against the Predators. He signed a new two-year contract this past summer that converts to a one-way deal next season.</p><p>Soderblom, meanwhile, has long been a scapegoat for fans, many of whom welcomed Sunday's transaction yet wished bigger news had accompanied it.</p><p>He has an .885 save percentage across 117 career NHL games, and he has been particularly poor early this season, losing each of his four starts and posting an .842 save percentage in them. He most recently allowed several soft goals that doomed the Hawks to a 4-1 loss <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/05/blackhawks-lightning-arvid-soderblom-backup-goalie" >Thursday</a> against the Lightning (then allowed three more goals in relief Saturday).</p><p>Since the start of last season, Soderblom's minus-18.2 GSAA ranks sixth-worst in the NHL, per Natural Stat Trick. That means he has allowed 18.2 more goals than expected based on the quantity and quality of shots he has faced.</p><p>There's no guarantee Commesso turns out to be an improvement over Soderblom — particularly behind a defense this weak — but it's hard to imagine him being worse. It's almost certainly worth a shot.</p><p>Commesso said in training camp that knowing he belongs at the NHL level has allowed him to "carry myself a little differently in a lot of good ways."</p><p>The Hawks placed Patrick Kane on injured reserve to open the roster spot, but he's eligible to be activated at any time.</p>
entries.author: Ben Pope

entries.title: LeBron James becomes player with most career points against Bulls
entries.summary: <p>LeBron James did what he does against the Bulls on Sunday — score.</p><p>James hit his first bucket of the game, a three-pointer, to give him the most career points of anyone against the Bulls. He finished with 22 points and now has 1,916 in 70 career games.</p><p>He told reporters that he had no idea that he had done it. The NBA posted his accomplishment on social media. Otherwise, perhaps no one would’ve known.</p><p>“He’s still an elite player,” Bulls coach Tiago Splitter said. “We battled a couple of times on the court, [NBA] Finals and all that. He probably has the best career ever. Can’t believe that he’s still doing this. We have the same age, and I’m here coaching.”</p><p>James, 41, is in his 24th NBA season and first with the 76ers, his fourth team. He has played against the Bulls more than any other team, thanks to his 15 seasons with the Eastern Conference-rival Cavaliers and Heat. He has played 69 games against the Pacers and Pistons. James will face the Bulls two more times this season, the next coming Jan. 23 in Chicago.</p><p>His eventual Hall of Fame career includes four NBA championships, four NBA Finals MVP Awards and four regular-season MVP Awards. He also became the league’s all-time scoring leader in 2023, when he passed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.</p><h3>Claxton returns from injury</h3><p>Center Nic Claxton made his long-awaited return from a hamstring injury he suffered in the first week of training camp. With a restriction on his minutes, Claxton had four points, four rebounds and four assists in over 17 minutes.</p><p>“I needed the restriction today,” Claxton said. “I was a little tired.”</p><p>“He was gassed out there, which is normal for his first real game after a month,” Splitter said.</p><p>“I think Nic had issues on the boards there with [Joel] Embiid and the other guys. [Jabari] Walker grabbed a bunch, too.”</p><p>Claxton said he didn’t feel any effects from the injury, which he said was his first time dealing with a strained muscle. Claxton, an eighth-year veteran, is in the third year of a four-year, $97 million contract he signed with the Nets. The Bulls acquired him in a trade in June.</p><p>“I just wanted to finish the game,” he said. “You see people coming back and in their first game they’re getting them. So I’m happy that I’m all good.”</p><h3>Essengue making strides</h3><p>Forward Noa Essengue, the Bulls’ 2025 first-round pick, had 10 points, scoring in double figures for the second time this season. He was very active, pulling down seven rebounds, including three on offense, and contesting shots. But he still has a ways to go in his development.</p><p>“Noa is a young fellow that is learning how to pressure the ball, how to navigate screens,” Splitter said. “I thought that he had good moments on their guys. Of course, he made some mistakes.”</p><p>Essengue played with Claxton, who has been impressed with the youngster, the last first-round pick made by the previous regime under Arturas Karnisovas.</p><p>“He has all the intangibles — quickness, length,” Claxton said. “Now he’s got to put it all together. He’s got a lot of room to grow, but I think he can be great in the league.</p><p>“It’s impressive how he’s able to pick up guards full court at 6-9, 6-10. A lot of dudes can’t do that. That’s one of his superpowers.”</p><h3>Collins still sick</h3><h3></h3><p>Center Zach Collins didn’t play because of a respiratory illness. He had missed the last two days of practice, as well.</p>
entries.author: Jeff Agrest

entries.title: Josh Giddey gives Bulls' offense a lift by going downhill
entries.summary: <p>Bulls point guard Josh Giddey is painfilly aware of his slow start to the season. His shooting percentage and scoring average are well below where he finished last season, and he said he still was trying to figure out how to be effective in the offense.</p><p>“I’ve probably played the worst eight games that I’ve played in my career, in terms of the stretch,” he said last week after practice.</p><p>If that’s the case, then he snapped that skid Sunday, scoring 19 points and handing out 15 assists in the Bulls’ 127-121 loss to the 76ers. The assists marked a season high and were four short of his career high.</p><p>Giddey said last week that the Bulls needed to start faster and he needed to play more downhill, rather than laterally. Both happened against a Sixers team that entered the game fourth in the NBA in defensive efficiency.</p><p>“He was the Josh that we know,” coach Tiago Splitter said. “He was aggressive. He was driving downhill, getting teammates [involved], and that’s how we see this game. We got to touch the paint and find options out there.”</p><p>Touching the paint is crucial for the Bulls’ offense. Giddey said the their points per possession is much higher when they get in the lane. Of course, it also helps when they make shots. The Bulls shot a season-high 52.3% from the field, their first game over 50% this season.</p><p>“Guys made shots, and they make my job easy,” Giddey said. “It doesn’t just have to be me. We look really good when we hit the paint. It’s just a matter of continuing to do that and not settle for contested stuff early. That’s where we can get in trouble.”</p><p>The Bulls appeared to be in trouble before the game when they learned that guard Norman Powell, their second-leading scorer, had developed back spasms in the morning and would be unavailable. That put defensive specialist Isaac Okoro in the lineup, and he delivered on offense, as well, scoring 12 points.</p><p>“Naturally, we have a better defensive team with Isaac in there,” Splitter said. “He did a good job offensively, as well, driving, cutting, back doors, and-ones.”</p><p>Matas Buzelis had 19 points, Caleb Wilson 18 and Jalen Smith 17 to round out the starters. Noa Essengue had 10 points off the bench.</p><p>It started with Giddey, who set the tone on the Bulls’ first possession by driving and feeding Okoro for a layup. He drove for his own layups, as well, including one on a Euro step. He later dished to Smith for a layup.</p><p>Giddey had seven assists in the first six minutes, and the Bulls had 13 field goals in the first quarter, their most this season.</p><p>But the game also ended with Giddey, who committed two turnovers down the stretch. He made up for one by setting up Wilson for a three-pointer that cut the Sixers’ lead to 116-113. He made another later with the Bulls down five. Giddey had five turnovers for the game.</p><p>“Against a team like that, the margin for error is so small,” he said. “I had a couple turnovers late that I would’ve wanted back. But I thought we competed a lot better than we have the last few games.”</p><p>Indeed they did. Thought there are no moral victories in the NBA, against a Sixers team that entered with an Eastern Conference-leading 8-2 record, the Bulls can take some solace in defeat.</p><p>“We stepped up,” Splitter said. “Our guys competed for the most part. At the end of the day, the game is decided on the boards. They got 20 offensive boards. We did a lot of good things. Played the way we want to play. It wasn’t enough. That’s a very good team.”</p><p>And another one is coming to town Wednesday, when the 8-2 Spurs visit. The Bulls’ season-opening gauntlet continues.</p>
entries.author: Jeff Agrest

entries.title: Packers force 4 turnovers in 45-27 win over Patriots
entries.summary: <p>FOXBOROUGH, Mass. — Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns and ran for a score, and the Green Bay Packers scored 21 points off four New England Patriots turnovers to roll to a 45-27 win on Sunday.</p><p>Green Bay's receivers had a huge day, with Christian Watson catching seven passes for 171 yards and a TD and Matthew Golden finishing with 10 catches for 164 yards and a score. Kaleb Johnson ran for a touchdown and Savion Williams had a TD catch as Green Bay finished with 478 total yards. The Packers hadn't scored 45 or more points and had 450 or more yards since Nov. 11, 1962 at Philadelphia.</p><p>Packers safety Xavier McKinney had a pair of interceptions and Evan Williams also had a pick.</p><p>Green Bay entered the day last in the NFL in rushing, averaging 60.6 yards per game, but finished with 129 yards on the ground.</p><p>The Packers (6-3) got plenty of help from the Patriots (5-4) as they built a 24-7 lead en route to their fifth win in six games.</p><p>New England's Drake Maye took a step backward after weeks of steady play, throwing three interceptions while completing 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards and three touchdowns. Maye had thrown just one pick in his previous four games.</p><p>The Patriots set a franchise record for points allowed at Gillette Stadium, which opened in 2002. New England hadn't given up 45 points in the regular season since a 45-7 loss to the New York Jets on Sept. 26, 1993.</p><p>Maye made questionable decisions on all three of his turnovers in the first half. Two of them set up Packers touchdowns. Rhamondre Stevenson, Efton Chism and Mack Hollins all had TD catches for the Patriots. Stevenson also had a fumble that set up Watson's score before leaving with a knee injury late third quarter.</p><p>DeMario Douglas caught five passes for 102 yards.</p><p>The Packers led 24-14 at halftime, then drove down the field on the opening possession of the second half. Love punctuated the seven-play, 70-yard drive with a 10-yard TD pass to Williams.</p><p>New England rookie Karon Prunty was in coverage on the score after Carlton Davis III suffered a knee injury in the second quarter.</p><p>Gillette Stadium was full of energy before the game as the Patriots celebrated members of their 2016 team — including an appearance by Tom Brady in the Fox broadcast booth — to commemorate the 10th anniversary of their record comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons in Super Bowl 51.</p><p>It quickly dissipated after the Patriots opened with a penalty, followed on the next play by Maye throwing the ball into traffic and being intercepted by McKinney at the New England 14.</p><p>Two plays later, Love easily found the end zone on a scramble and the Packers jumped in front 7-0.</p><p>Green Bay never trailed.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Packers:</b> Linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper left early in the first quarter with a chest injury. Running back Josh Jacobs left later in the quarter with a hand injury. ... Wide receiver Bo Melton was evaluated for a concussion.</p><p><b>Patriots:</b> Left guard Ben Brown (knee) limped off a few plays after Davis late in the second quarter. ... Special teamer Brenden Schooler exited with a hamstring injury. ... Left tackle Will Campbell walked off with a knee injury in the fourth quarter.</p><h3>Packers’ receiving duo has rare achievement</h3><h3></h3><p>Watson and Golden became the first Packers teammates to have 150 or more receiving yards and a touchdown catch since Don Hutson and Andy Uram did it in 1942.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Packers:</b> Host Minnesota next Sunday.</p><p><b>Patriots:</b> Travel to Germany to play Detroit next Sunday in Munich.<br></p>
entries.author: AP

entries.title: Bears can't win sizzling NFC North unless they do their own dirty work and beat their rivals themselves
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ NFL brethren didn’t do them any favors Sunday.</p><p>Certainly not the amateur-hour Dolphins, who held down Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions’ No. 1-ranked offense admirably enough but never really threatened in a 19-9 loss in Miami Gardens, Florida.</p><p>And — in surprisingly feckless fashion — not the defending AFC champion Patriots, either. Hosting the Packers, the Pats were total no-shows in an embarrassing 45-27 defeat, with Fox analyst Tom Brady in the house to binge-watch long Jordan Love completions and wince-worthy Drake Maye interceptions in his return to Foxborough, Massachusetts.</p><p>What ever happened to doing the Bears a solid? Well, it so happens that’s not the rest of the league’s job.</p><p>The day’s events leading into the Bears’ kickoff against the Buccaneers at Soldier Field were good reminders of a couple of important things.</p><p>One, the NFC North is ridiculously good.</p><p>It is, of course, unique among the league’s divisions in that all its teams have winning records; each had six wins, in fact, heading into Bears-Bucs and the Vikings’ Monday-nighter at home against the AFC-favorite Bills. The table is set for the best, most compelling division race in the NFL the rest of the regular season.</p><p>Underscoring just how much better the Bears’ division is than the competition: The Packers’ big win raised the North’s aggregate record against outside foes this season to a dizzyingly good 19-3. The Bears were already 6-0 in that department before taking on the Bucs — and a truly hard-to-believe 15-2 in a season and a half under Ben Johnson — but that was merely allowing them to keep pace with their rivals after a pair of early, ugly division losses to the Vikings and the Packers. The Bears might be the betting favorites in the North these days, but any advantage is paper-thin.</p><p>The second, bigger thing: It might be the last major step separating them from the top of the NFL food chain, but the 2026 Bears are simply going to have to learn to do their own dirty work. Unlike last season, when crushing it outside the division enabled the Bears to finish in first place despite going 2-4 against the Lions, Vikings and Packers, there will be no division-title repeat unless the Bears stand up to the rivals who have bullied them without mercy since 2019, the last year the Bears managed a winning record against the North.</p><p>The Bears have lost seven of their last eight games against the Lions and nine of their last 11 against the Vikings. Nobody needs to be reminded of how lopsided things long have been against the Packers. Starting in 2020, the Bears have been in an overall 9-29 mega-slide in the North.</p><p>A Thanksgiving game in Detroit will be a major challenge. The three game gauntlet to end the regular season — Packers, Lions and Vikings, in that order — will tell all. The Bears won’t be able to juke their way through it or fake their way around it.</p><p>And what happens to the Bears' chances if all four North teams make the playoffs? It would be a first for any division, but it could happen.</p><p>No matter how strong the Bears end up being outside the North, the bigger reveal will be what lies for them within it.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-inactives-bears-rb-kyle-monangai-remains-out-with-toe-injury" target="_blank" >Halftime: Bears lead Buccaneers 17-6 despite Caleb Williams’ career-high 3 interceptions</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/what-to-watch-for-in-buccaneers-bears-game-sunday-a-new-test-for-the-bears-rebuilt-defensive-line" >What to watch for in Buccaneers-Bears game Sunday: A new test for the Bears’ rebuilt defensive line</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-mike-tirico-out-health-sunday-night-football-nbc-annoncer" >Bears-Bucs notes: Mike Tirico sits out with health issue</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Body pulled from Chicago River in Albany Park
entries.summary: <p>A man's body was pulled out of the Chicago River Sunday afternoon in Albany Park on the Northwest Side.</p><p>The body was recovered from the water around 1:20 p.m. in the 3000 block of West Argyle Street, according to Chicago police. </p><p>He was pronounced dead at the scene, police said. His name, age and other details have not been released. </p>

entries.title: Dancing Ben Johnson shows Bears players 'he’s just one of us'
entries.summary: <p>Ben Johnson had just handed out game balls to three <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> players after their Monday night win in Seattle when Kyler Gordon reached out and slapped a sticker on his coach’s chest.</p><p>It was a sticker of Johnson doing the Stanky Legg, a dance craze the coach jump-started the last time the Bears won on Monday night, in Week 3. Deciding to dance after they beat the Eagles was a “panic move,” Johnson said with a smile.</p><p>The dance first became popular when GS Boyz released a rap song of the same name in 2008, when Johnson was 22. The video of the coach dancing now accompanies the team’s “Good, Better, Best” social media videos after victories and has inspired everything from T-shirts to the stickers handed to Gordon in Seattle. Johnson had one on slapped his chest by the slot cornerback before he started dancing Monday. He stuck his left leg out, bent at 90 degrees, and slapped his knee with his right hand, causing it to wobble.</p><p>What’s remarkable about Johnson letting loose is the contrast between the coach pregame and postgame. In the hours leading up to the kickoff, Johnson walls himself off emotionally. He studies the call sheet, often alone. He doesn’t speak much, even to his own coaching staff. Once the game starts, he wants his coaches speaking on his headset as little as is necessary.</p><p>After the game, he’s different.</p><p>“It shows everybody that he’s just one of us …” receiver Rome Odunze said. “He wants to be precise, he wants to go out there and execute. But man, this game is about having fun and going out there and winning games. I think, like, that’s his expression of all that. We all feel that, for sure.”</p><p>That connection is vital for the first-time head coach. Johnson doesn’t hesitate to yell at his players when things aren’t going the right way. Film sessions can be tough, even after — actually, especially after — the team wins. But he knows he can’t keep his intensity up all the time. Loosening up allows him to connect with his players.</p><p>The result has been a resounding success. Johnson entered Sunday night’s home game against the Buccaneers with a chance to, with a win, move past George Halas on the Bears’ all-time winning percentage. It’s a small sample size, but impressive nonetheless. </p><p>He entered Sunday’s game needed just three wins the rest of the season to set the Bears’ all-time record for most victories in the first two years of a head coach’s career.</p><p>When the Bears hired Johnson, there was no question he knew how to call offensive plays. The bigger issue was how he would act as the head coach, on and off the field. Could he be a leader? Could he inspire? Could he connect?</p><p>The answer has been a resounding yes.</p><p>Almost every head coaching hire the Bears have ever made has come with the same question. In franchise history, the Bears have hired only two men with previous head coach experience — John Fox and Paddy Driscoll, though the latter had a player-coach stint on his resume.</p><p>Every other hire, from the good (Mike Ditka and Lovie Smith) to the bad (everyone else), has come with questions about what they’d look like as the person in charge.</p><p>Johnson’s emotional intelligence is one of the many things that set Johnson apart from his predecessors. Matt Eberflus was seemed rarely at ease — perhaps because of the team’s record. Matt Nagy was comfortable in his own skin, but both he and his “Club Dub” creation grew tired when the team stopped winning as much as it did in 2018.</p><p>Johnson gave a glimpse of that self-awareness in his first spring with the team, when he recited a poem about Brian Piccolo before the team’s annual Piccolo Awards. He’s remained the same way, even during the stresses of the season. His decision to rip his shirt off during a “Black Friday” locker room celebration last year amused his players — and fed Chicagoans free hot dogs. Hearing Johnson talk about how much he hated the Packers — in colorful language — fed Bears fans on a spiritual level.</p><p>The intensity, though, is never too far from the surface.</p><p>That’s why quarterback Caleb Williams can, with a smile, reference “a genius like Ben — and a psycho like Ben” in his pregame interview with NBC.</p><p>When the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons last week, the defensive tackle admitted that the only thing he really knew about Johnson was the fact that he yapped at him during a joint practice in August</p><p>“We talked a little smack back and forth when they came to visit Tennessee,” he said. “But I'm excited to know what he's doing with this team and what he's building here.”<br></p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Might looming lockout spark early flurry of offseason activity as Cubs head to GM meetings in Las Vegas?
entries.summary: <p>Baseball’s GM meetings are rarely the site of big-money free-agent deals and blockbuster trades.</p><p>But might this year’s edition, happening this week in Las Vegas, be different?</p><p>With what’s expected to be a lengthy lockout looming, there’s a curiosity over whether these GM meetings could function more like the winter meetings, when all that wheeling and dealing typically takes place, a month later on the baseball calendar.</p><p>Instead of merely setting the table for the offseason to come, though, might front offices across the sport treat this week as the starting gun for a sprint to the start of December, when baseball is expected to be forced into hibernation, all free-agent and trade activity placed on pause?</p><p>Though he probably has a better idea of what’s to come than he did a month ago, when he held his end-of-season news conference far earlier than hoped, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> president Jed Hoyer has to navigate those waters as he looks to start checking items off his winter to-do list.</p><p>“We’ll make the best decisions with the information we have at the time,” he said last month. “Some of those may come before Dec. 1, and some may come after. But I don’t think anyone, at this point, has a firm grasp on that. If they say they do, they’re probably incorrect.”</p><p>The last time baseball endured a work stoppage, between the 2021 and 2022 seasons, there was a lot of free-agent activity in November, with some pretty big contracts handed out leading up to the clock striking midnight and everything being put on hold.</p><p>This week’s GM meetings could signal whether teams will operate similarly this time around, seeking security in what their rosters will look like, regardless of how negotiations over a collective-bargaining agreement play out.</p><p>“If there are contracts that will make sense no matter the setup, then you make those deals,’’ Hoyer said. ‘‘There are certainly going to be contracts that make sense regardless of the structure. Knowing what is going to be after, you’re making a lot of assumptions.</p><p>“But certainly there are deals, contracts, players that you would retain regardless of what that structure was.”</p><p>Whether they get it all done before the buzzer sounds or after the lockout, whenever that might be, Hoyer & Co. have a lot of work to do.</p><p>Chiefly, there’s remaking the Cubs’ pitching staff, the undoubted priority for the front office in the wake of a disappointing playoff exit. All five of the pitchers who finished the season in the rotation are free agents, and Hoyer was blunt in his assessment that his work to construct a bullpen last winter didn’t work, forecasting a makeover there, too.</p><p>“It’s safe to say that the biggest part of our focus going into the offseason is going to be on pitching,” Hoyer said. “Whether that’s 100-to-0, what that ratio is going to be, has not been determined yet. But certainly, the great majority of our focus is going to be on pitching acquisition going in.”</p><p>There are potential needs on the far more stable position-player side, too, with corner outfielders Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki — the latter got a qualifying offer from the Cubs last week — potentially departing as free agents.</p><p>Over the last calendar year, Hoyer has not been shy about making win-now trades, shipping top prospects away in exchange for Edward Cabrera, Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes. The latter two were acquired as trade-deadline rentals but didn’t help the Cubs even make it to October; the team was swept out of the wild-card round.</p><p>But those were the kinds of bets Hoyer’s front office needed to make to push a team built to win toward championship contention.</p><p>As expectations remain at the championship level, the question will be how much is left in the farm system to make similar deals?</p><p>Should there not be enough to lure away top talent from other clubs, perhaps the coffers will have to open once again, the way they did to land Alex Bregman last offseason.</p><p>Bregman proved worth every penny of his $175 million free-agent contract, awakening from a deep slump in dramatic enough fashion to finish as the Cubs’ second-best hitter and playing Gold Glove defense at third base.</p><p>Those are the things Hoyer has done, and while he made the moves necessary to set the Cubs up for success, they didn’t equal success in the end. So it’s back to the drawing board to make the improvements that will not just get the Cubs another crack at the postseason but position them to challenge for division, league and MLB championships, an even taller task now that the division rival Brewers are kings of the baseball world.</p><p>The quest for pitching likely already has begun for Hoyer & Co., and perhaps the hot stove gets flipped on a little early with the lockout on the way.</p><p>We’ll find out this week.</p>

entries.title: Bears' grades are in. How did they do against the Buccaneers?
entries.summary: <p>Five turnovers, four of them interceptions thrown by Caleb Williams. Some worrisome injuries, too.</p><p>That the Bears won 27-24 against the Buccaneers to get to 7-2 is the main thing — it is, isn't it? — but, in a bubble, the Bears looked like anything but a Super Bowl contender. They'll just have to take it and move into a bye week. Whew, a bye — right on time.</p><p>Let's get the the Bears' grades:</p><h3><b>QUARTERBACK — C-MINUS</b></h3><p>Just when NBC’s Cris Collinsworth was so beside himself with excitement over Caleb Williams’ play that he likened the third-year star to Joe Montana, the second quarter hit. Hoo boy. After a first-quarter performance that came as close as it gets to breathtaking, Williams suddenly regressed into Montana’s 49ers predecessor, Steve DeBerg, who threw 60 interceptions in three seasons before the great Montana took over in 1981. Williams’ three-INT second quarter was shockingly bad, each pick worse than the one before it. The fastballs for big gains downfield might drop jaws, but throwing balls up for grabs while backpedaling? Seriously? But Williams at least climbed from a D grade by driving the Bears for the winning field goal.</p><h3><b>RECEIVERS — B-MINUS</b></h3><p>There can’t be a sight more glorious for Bears fans to behold than Luther Burden crossing over the middle for a routine-looking grab four yards past the line of scrimmage, then planting, exploding upfield and running 52 yards after the catch — through three would-be tacklers — for a touchdown. On the other hand, there aren’t many worse sights than Burden taking a knockout hit and fumbling late in the fourth quarter. Fellow wide receiver Rome Odunze bobbled an absolutely perfect pass in the back of the end zone, but Williams came back to him on third down from the 9 for the Bears’ first score. Odunze’s honorary home-run swing and “We love you, boy!” into the camera for injured tight end Cole Kmet earned a few extra-credit points. Wideout Zavion Thomas hurt the cause with a personal foul that pushed the Bears out of the red zone and led to Williams’ first INT.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">No WR came into the week with more broken tackles than Luther Burden <a href="https://t.co/zcn327A72u">pic.twitter.com/zcn327A72u</a></p>— PFF (@PFF) <a href="https://x.com/PFF/status/2119607447686111323?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 9, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>OFFENSIVE LINE — C-MINUS</b></h3><p>Williams didn’t take a lot of hard hits, but he was under instant pressure on far too many drop-backs. On one such play — and there were many — left tackle Theo Benedet completely whiffed on Bucs rookie Rueben Bain’s third-down rush off the edge; Williams had to chuck the ball into the ground and the Bears had to settle for a 25-yard field goal. Running game? What running game?</p><h3><b>RUN DEFENSE — B</b></h3><p>Against the top rushing attack in the NFL, the “D” was outstanding most of the way. Repeatedly, linebacker Devin Bush — who had his best game as a Bear — shot into gaps and blew up runs. End Austin Booker crashed down on multiple occasions and eliminated runs before they got started. Bucky Irving finished strong, though, with 97 yards, two TDs and 4.9 per carry in all.</p><h3><b>PASS DEFENSE — A-MINUS</b></h3><p>Nickel corner Kyler Gordon and rookie safety Dillon Thieneman were toasted on a 58-yard pass from Baker Mayfield to Tez Johnson at the start of the third quarter, setting up a Bucs touchdown that made it 17-13. But versatile Cam Lewis jumped a Mayfield pass for a pick and — we’ve buried the lede — beleaguered corner Jaylon Johnson finally got to beat his chest after a 67-yard pick-six. The rush picked up late, with Jeffrey Simmons, Shemar Turner, Grady Jarrett, Daniel Hardy and Booker all ending up in the sacks column.</p><h3><b>SPECIAL TEAMS — D</b></h3><p>Tory Taylor had another punt blocked. A D’Marco Jackson hold — questionable, but a hold — brought back a 91-yard kickoff return by Zavion Thomas. Upback Jack Sanborn’s false start spoiled an attempt at a fake punt that, if we’re being honest, wasn’t going to work anyway. The Bears always look like they’re ready to break a huge return, but the mistakes are mounting. Thank goodness Cairo Santos drilled the walk-off winner from 38 yards.</p><h3><b>TOMORROW’S HEADLINES</b></h3><p><b>Bye, Bye, Bears: </b>No game this weekend — a very good thing, because this team needs a break. A lot of guys have a lot of mistakes to think about and correct.</p><p><b>A Confident QB? </b>Caleb<b> </b>Williams is the key to the whole operation, but is he rattled after throwing four picks? He’ll say no, of course, but it’s a legit concern.</p><p><b>Injury Updates: </b>Getting Kyle Monangai back out of the bye would be a godsend. Will Luther Burden miss time? Oh, no — Kyler Gordon hurt again?</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-inactives-bears-rb-kyle-monangai-remains-out-with-toe-injury" target="_blank" >Bears survive Caleb Williams’ 4 interceptions to beat Buccaneers 27-24 on Cairo Santos’ late field goal</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-packers-lions-vikings-patriots-nfc-north-nfl-best-division" >Bears can’t win sizzling NFC North unless they do their own dirty work and beat their rivals themselves</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-kyler-gordon-leaves-game-with-injury" >Bears CB Kyler Gordon leaves game with injury, returns</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Bears CB Kyler Gordon leaves game with injury, returns
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>' need for cornerback help before Tuesday's trade deadline might have just gotten more serious.</p><p>Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon, whose four sacks in three games this season made him Dennis Allen's most successful blitzer, left Sunday night's game <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-inactives-bears-rb-kyle-monangai-remains-out-with-toe-injury" target="_blank" >against the Buccaneers</a> with an injury. He returned later in the third quarter.</p><p> In the first half, outside cornerback Tyrique Stevenson left the game with a hand injury. He returned, too, midway through the third quarter.</p><p>Gordon was injured while chasing down Tez Johnson, whose 58-yard catch and run gave the Bucs the ball at the Bears' 2. He was in considerable pain after tackling Johnson, went to the blue injury tent and then the locker room. He held his left arm in front of his belly gingerly. The Buccaneers scored two plays later.</p><p>Stevenson took himself out of the game and appeared to be in pain, too. He was replaced by Clark Phillips, whom the Bears acquired in the Gervon Dexter trade during training camp. </p><p>Cam Lewis moved from safety to slot cornerback to take Gordon's place, with Elijah Hicks entering at safety.</p><p>Struggles by Jaylon Johnson and an injury to Malik Muhammad meant the Bears were already considered to be buyers at cornerback before the deadline, which is Tuesday at 3 p.m. <br></p>

entries.title: Bears' Cairo Santos 'had to have my teammates’ backs' with game-winner
entries.summary: <p>At some point during the ugly <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>-Buccaneers tussle Sunday night at Soldier Field, kicker Cairo Santos turned to his teammates on the bench at made a declaration: at some point the game would be tied, probably something like 20-20, and the Bears would need to find a way to win it.</p><p>He was mostly right. The game was knotted at 24 when Santos swung his right leg for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-inactives-bears-rb-kyle-monangai-remains-out-with-toe-injury" target="_blank" >game-winning 38-yard field goal</a> as time expired.</p><p>“I had to have my teammates’ backs,” Santos said. “The important thing is we got out of here with a win.”</p><p>Santos’ kick was set up by a 38-yard yard pass from Caleb Williams to Colston Loveland on busted Buccaneers coverage to get the ball to the 16. Caleb Williams kneeled twice, putting the ball at the right hash mark, where Santos liked it.</p><p>Santos has now made seven game-winning kicks in the final two minutes or overtime, which is the third-most in Bears history. Kevin Butler and Robbie Gould are tied for the lead with 10 apiece.</p><p>“Confidence is key,” Santos said. “It’s, dating back to last year, the identity we’ve been building.”</p>

entries.title: Bears defense saves the day vs. Buccaneers
entries.summary: <p>Yes, the ball landed in their cornerbacks’ arms, at times, as though it had been flown in via remote control.</p><p>Yes, the opposing receivers dropped passes like they the ball was made of molten lava.</p><p>But say this: the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> built a defense that could win a game when their offense was just as bad Sunday night. The Bears beat the Buccaneers 27-24 in a slopfest because their defense overcame their offense.</p><p>The Bucs helped, of course. They had five false starts. Their quarterback, Baker Mayfield, was worse than Caleb Williams.</p><p>But the defense carrying the team to victory would have seemed impossible after Week 1, when the Bears outscored the Panthers 59-37, or Week 5, when the Packers hung 31 on the Bears.</p><p>They improved to 7-2 despite Williams, whose four interceptions doubled his previous career high, and in spite of penalties that cost the Bears a kickoff return touchdown and, perhaps, a successful fake punt. They won despite the Bears going the entire third quarter without a first down.</p><p>Credit cornerback Jaylon Johnson, whose struggles this season have been myriad and well-documented, returning a Mayfield pass 67 yards for a touchdown with about four minutes left in the third quarter. He ran up the left flank and into the north end zone for the second pick-six of his career, and first since 2023.</p><p>Montez Sweat was his lead blocker, shoving Mayfield out of the way at the 15.</p><p>Asked what he told Sweat, Johnson smiled and said, simply, “Thank you.”</p><p>The Bears’ offense turned the ball over five times. Their defense gave up 11 points on the Bucs’ ensuing drives, with the lone touchdown coming after Luther Burden fumbled at the Bears’ 17 with 3:38 left in the game. He was concussed on the play.</p><p>“That was really the story of the game — those guys stepping up,” coach Ben Johnson said.</p><p>The Bears led 14-0 less than nine minutes into the game but watched their play degrade by the second. When Johnson intercepted the pass, the Bears were ahead by just four points. Soldier Field exhaled.</p><p>“That’s just who we are — we always fight,” said Jaylon Johnson, who got the only game ball handed out by his head coach.</p><p>Credit Cam Lewis, who started at safety and shuffled to slot cornerback when Kyler Gordon was briefly hurt in the third quarter, picked off Mayfield at the Bears’ 34 in the second quarter.</p><p>And credit Jeffery Simmons, the Bears’ best defensive player, who ran a longer distance during the entirety of the first half than Bucs running back Bucky Irving. He sacked Mayfield with about six minutes left in the fourth quarter, one play after Austin Booker’s third-down sack was wiped out by the fact he grabbed Mayfield’s facemask. One play after Simmons’ sack, Daniel Hardy and Grady Jarrett shared a sack. Two plays later, the Bucs, down by eight, were forced to punt with about 4:30 to play.</p><p>Simmons said he was double-teamed 99% of the time, but he found a way to make an impact.</p><p>“How can I affect the game when I’m not hitting the quarterback?” he said. “When I’m not getting tackles for loss in the backfield? When teams know they’re not running the ball inside and are bouncing the ball outside. How can I be around the football? I took a lot of pride in being around the football. You just never know. The ball may pop out. I can force a fumble. I can save a touchdown just by running to the ball.”</p><p>Sunday, they needed every ounce of his energy to win the game.</p><p>"Once we put a complete game together, good luck," Simmons said.</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Bears' Jeffery Simmons: Fans' orange tribute was 'amazing'
entries.summary: <p>Jeffery Simmons’ social media timeline told him of the plan by <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> fans Sunday night: to wear orange to welcome him to his first game at Soldier Field.</p><p>When the defensive tackle ran out of the tunnel wearing his trademark orange sleeves, he looked around and saw the same hue worn by many in the stands.</p><p>“That was amazing …” he said after the Bears’ <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-inactives-bears-rb-kyle-monangai-remains-out-with-toe-injury" target="_blank" >27-24 win against the Buccaneers</a>. “I’m very appreciative. … The fans were amazing today, especially in the fourth quarter when we really needed them. …</p><p>“That was pretty sweet to see coming out of the tunnel there.”</p><p>He said he underestimated the impact playing in his new home would have on him.</p><p>“It was amazing to run out the first time at Soldier Field,” he said.</p><p>Simmons finished the game with one sack and four tackles despite being double teamed, in his estimation, “99% of the day.”<br></p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams on 4-interception game vs. Bucs: 'Going to keep gripping it and keep ripping it'
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback Caleb Williams played one of the worst games of his career Sunday against the Buccaneers and still <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/08/bears-buccaneers-inactives-bears-rb-kyle-monangai-remains-out-with-toe-injury" >got away with a 27-24 win</a>.</p><p>Williams threw a career-high four interceptions — he’d never thrown more than two — and completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards with two touchdowns for a 61.5 passer rating. Those mistakes, as well as a lost fumble late in the game by wide receiver Luther Burden, prevented the Bears from a runaway victory and left them needing a last-second, 38-yard field goal by Cairo Santos to win.</p><p>Williams came through on that final drive with a 38-yard pass to tight end Colston Loveland that got the Bears in field-goal range at the Bucs’ 16-yard line.</p><p>“I’m going to throw until I can’t throw anymore,” he said. “That’s how I live. That’s how I grew up. That’s what I am. I don’t get gun shy. I’m going to keep gripping it and keep ripping it.”</p><p>Williams was critical of his play, which included three interceptions in the first half after jumping out to a 14-0 lead. The Bears easily could’ve gone into halftime up 20 or more points, but instead led 17-6 and allowed the Bucs to pull within 17-13 early in the third quarter.</p><p>Williams described his first interception, a throw to the end zone for wide receiver Rome Odunze as “greedy.” On the next two, which came on consecutive passes, he let the Bucs’ pass rush pressure him into bad decisions. The fourth interception, in the third quarter, was tipped at the line.</p><p>“Just tried to be the big eraser,” Williams said. “That’s what I’ve been. That’s what I will be. Today, I wasn’t.”</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser
